claims.text: Increasing Al content or the Al/Cr ratio promotes preferential formation of a coherent, slow-growing Al2O3 surface layer.
The Al2O3 layer remains protective and stable above 900 °C in oxidative or corrosive environments.
Alloys with lower Al content or relatively higher Mn/Si form mixed oxide scales.
The mixed scales formed by lower-Al or higher-Mn/Si alloys are less adherent and tend to crack or spall.
A continuous Al2O3 scale acts as a diffusion barrier between the alloy and the environment.
Higher Al content favors selective oxidation of Al over Cr or Mn.
Selective oxidation of Al over Cr or Mn occurs because Al has a lower diffusion coefficient.
Al2O3 scales grow more slowly than chromium oxide scales.
Al oxides are thermodynamically stable relative to Fe, Co, and Ni oxides.
Al2O3 is mechanically compatible with the substrate and therefore minimizes scale stresses.
Minimizing scale stresses reduces cracking and spallation.
Lower Al content permits formation of chromia or Mn-rich oxides that are less adherent and more susceptible to failure.
Above 900 °C, chromia can form volatile CrO3.
The lower-Al baseline is expected to form high-temperature scales containing Cr-, Mn-, and Fe-bearing oxides.
Enhanced-Al alloys will exhibit less cracking and spallation than the baseline under otherwise similar exposure conditions.
The proposed behavior applies broadly to single- or multiphase CrFeCoNiX solid solutions above 900 °C in oxidative or corrosive atmospheres.
Phase separation, compositional gradients, and microstructural heterogeneity can alter oxide-scale formation and limit the proposed behavior.

contradictions.description: The intervention says that other elemental concentrations are held constant while Mn or Si is replaced by Al. Replacement necessarily changes at least the replaced element's concentration, so both conditions cannot hold simultaneously.

A nominal Al baseline is assumed for the entire CrFeCoNiX family, but compositions with X = Si or Mn do not contain Al under the stated five-element notation. The baseline and substitution path therefore require an unstated Al-containing composition definition.
